title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

target.split: Test = 50% of documents not used as normal training data (normal + anomalous); token-level scoring over test documents

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

requirements.stmt: Word-level token embeddings must be formed by element-wise max pooling over the embeddings of all subwords of that word (Equation 1), not by taking the first subword or averaging.
requirements.cite: Section 5, Embedding Extraction with Max Pooling, Eq. (1)
requirements.quote: To maximize the anomaly signal for each token, we propose using max pooling to aggregate subword embeddings.

requirements.stmt: A memory bank must be built from the word-level embeddings of all tokens in the normal training documents only (no anomalous-token embeddings are stored).
requirements.quote: we extract word-level embeddings from all normal samples in the training set and store them in a memory bank

requirements.stmt: The token-level anomaly score is the minimum distance from the test-token embedding to any memory-bank entry (Equation 2); larger distance means more anomalous.
requirements.quote: we compute its anomaly score as the distance to its nearest neighbor in the memory bank

requirements.stmt: Document-level anomaly scores must be obtained by mean aggregation of the token-level scores over all tokens of the document (Equation 3).
requirements.quote: To obtain document-level anomaly scores, we aggregate token-level scores across all tokens in the document.

why: The authors released the method code (TokenCore.py: memory bank + nearest-neighbor token scoring), the alignment/annotation utilities (align.py, tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py) and all three annotated datasets locally in data/ (grammar .npy/.json, restaurant_review, sms_spam), so the core logic can be kept verbatim. What is NOT released is a runnable entrypoint: the only end-to-end artifact is Demo.ipynb (with frozen outputs), there is no requirements.txt, and TokenCore.py consumes precomputed token-embedding matrices, so the BERT-base-uncased embedding extraction, the 50/50 split and the token-level AUROC computation have to be rebuilt as a script from the notebook before the target number for Grammar (C1) can be produced. Keep authors' logic, rebuild the missing driver.
est_runtime: ~25-35 min wall clock on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM: ~10 min installing torch (CPU wheel), transformers, scikit-learn; ~1 min BERT-base download; ~1-3 min BERT forward pass over 300 short Grammar documents; seconds for the max-pooling, memory-bank build and brute-force nearest-neighbor scoring; plus the driver-script rewrite from the notebook and one clean end-to-end re-run.
blockers: no dependency file: torch/transformers/sklearn/numpy must be pinned by hand (works on Python 3.12)
TokenCore.py takes embedding matrices only; the BERT max-pooling-over-subwords front-end exists only inside the notebook, so the pipeline must be extracted into a script
Demo.ipynb is 3.8 MB of stored outputs; it must be rewritten/cleared before execution
no GPU on this machine (BERT-base CPU inference only, which is acceptable at this scale)

Grammar token-level AUROC is computed over very few anomalous tokens (~15 anomalous docs in the test half), and the split is random, so the absolute value 0.6371 will depend on the split seed and may drift

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.
steps: Clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git into ./TokenCore and record the commit hash; do not modify TokenCore.py, align.py or tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py.

Create a venv/conda env on Python 3.12 and pip install torch (CPU wheel from the default index), transformers, numpy, scikit-learn, tqdm, requests; write the resolved versions into requirements.txt (the file the README references but the repo lacks).

Run src/inspect_data.py: dump shapes/dtypes/keys of data/grammar.npy and the JSON schema of data/grammar_correction_labeled.json, and print the actual class/function signatures of TokenCore.py and align.py. Decide the exact field names for words, token labels and document labels, and confirm the .npy is a token/label array rather than precomputed embeddings (43 KB is far too small for 300x768 floats).

Implement src/data_grammar.py against the inspected schema; load all 300 Grammar documents and hard-assert 300 documents / 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% rate, R10) and consistency of the document labels with the token labels (R11).

Implement the split: with seed 0, shuffle the 270 normal documents, take the first 135 as the memory-bank training set; the test set is the other 135 normal documents plus all 30 anomalous documents (165 docs). Export the token-level gold labels for every test token.

Implement src/embed_bert.py: tokenize with BertTokenizerFast(return_offsets_mapping / word_ids), run BertModel in eval() with torch.no_grad() in batches of 32, max_length 128, take last_hidden_state, drop special tokens, and element-wise max-pool subwords per word unit. Assert a 1:1 map between produced word units and the gold word tokens in the annotated JSON; if align.py exposes an alignment helper, call it instead of re-implementing.

Implement src/detector.py: import the authors' TokenCore (use the real class name found by inspect_data.py, README shows both TokenCore and TextCore) and its fit / decision_function, fit on the normal-training token embedding matrix (no anomalous tokens, R3) and score the test token embeddings (R4).

Implement src/evaluate.py: token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro), document-level scores as the per-document mean of token scores (R5) and their AUROC/AUPRC, plus a random-score control (expected AUROC ~0.5) to validate the metric plumbing.
Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

If |token_auroc_grammar - 0.6371| > 0.02, re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and inspect sensitivity: report the per-seed values and mean/std, and check the highest-risk choices first (A5 micro vs per-document AUROC, A1/A9 Euclidean on unnormalized embeddings, A4 whether punctuation units are scored).
Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --smoke --seed 0 -> loads the released grammar annotations, keeps only the first 8 normal + first 2 anomalous documents (forcing the split so both sides are non-empty), runs one BERT-base forward pass over those 10 documents, max-pools subwords, builds a ~100-200 entry memory bank, scores the test tokens, and prints token_auroc/token_auprc plus every shape (n_docs, n_word_units, n_bank_tokens, n_test_tokens, n_positive_tokens). Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size and label rate: exactly 300 documents, 270 normal (token_labels all 0) and 30 anomalous (>=1 token_label = 1) = 10% anomaly rate (R10); stop if the released file deviates.
Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.
Alignment coverage: fraction of gold word tokens that receive a BERT word unit (target 1.0); log any word that tokenizes to zero subwords or overflows max_length=128.
Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Memory bank size: n_bank_tokens should equal the total number of word units in the 135 normal training documents (report it; expect a few thousand) - a much smaller number means documents were dropped silently.

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).
Metric parity: verify the AUROC/AUPRC implementation against sklearn.roc_auc_score / average_precision_score on synthetic labels, so the 0.6371 comparison cannot fail for plumbing reasons.
budget_plan: Total ~30-35 min on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM. Setup 10 min: clone the repo (<1 min) and pip install the CPU torch wheel plus transformers/scikit-learn (~8-9 min, ~5 GB, the dominant cost). Reconnaissance 3 min: inspect_data.py plus reading TokenCore.py/align.py and the JSON schema. Implementation 8 min: data_grammar.py, embed_bert.py, detector.py, evaluate.py, reproduce.py, requirements.txt. Smoke 2 min: 10-document subset end-to-end. Intermediate checks 2 min: counts, rates, alignment coverage, bank size, metric parity. Full run 3-4 min: one BERT-base forward pass over 300 short Grammar sentences on CPU (1-3 min) plus seconds of max-pooling and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour scoring. Verification 3 min: compare against 0.6371 with the ±0.02 band, and if out of band spend up to 5 more minutes on seeds 1 and 2 and on the highest-risk assumptions (A5, A1/A9, A4). Keep ~3 min slack; only the Grammar dataset is run, so no SMS_Spam/Review time is spent.

    5|     """
    6|     TokenCore anomaly detector based on nearest neighbor distances
    7|     """
    8|     def __init__(self, n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max'):
    9|         """
   10|         Parameters
   11|         ----------
   12|         n_neighbors : int, default=1
   13|             Number of neighbors to use
   14|         aggregation : str, default='mean'
   15|             How to aggregate distances when n_neighbors > 1
   16|             Options: 'mean', 'max', 'min', 'median'
   17|         """
   18|         self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
   19|         self.aggregation = aggregation
   20|         self.nbrs = None
   21|         
   22|     def fit(self, X):
   23|         """
   24|         Fit the model using X as training data
   25|         
   26|         Parameters
   27|         ----------
   28|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   29|             Training data
   30|             
   31|         Returns
   32|         -------
   33|         self : object
   34|             Fitted estimator
   35|         """
   36|         self.nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors).fit(X)
   37|         return self
   38|     
   39|     def decision_function(self, X):
   40|         """
   41|         Compute anomaly scores for samples in X
   42|         
   43|         Parameters
   44|         ----------
   45|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   46|             Test data
   47|             
   48|         Returns
   49|         -------
   50|         scores : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
   51|             Anomaly scores (higher means more anomalous)
   52|         """
   53|         distances, _ = self.nbrs.kneighbors(X)
   54|         
   55|         # If n_neighbors == 1, distances is (n_samples, 1), just flatten
   56|         if self.n_neighbors == 1:
   57|             scores = distances.flatten()
   58|         else:
   59|             # Aggregate multiple neighbor distances
   60|             if self.aggregation == 'mean':
   61|                 scores = np.mean(distances, axis=1)
   62|             elif self.aggregation == 'max':
   63|                 scores = np.max(distances, axis=1)
   64|             elif self.aggregation == 'min':
   65|                 scores = np.min(distances, axis=1)
   66|             elif self.aggregation == 'median':
   67|                 scores = np.median(distances, axis=1)
   68|             else:
   69|                 raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation method: {self.aggregation}")
   70|         
   71|         return scores

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |
   21|

"""
Load Grammar dataset and create train/test split.
"""
import numpy as np
import json
import os

def load_grammar(path='repo/data/grammar.npy'):
    """Load grammar dataset from .npy file."""
    data = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True).item()
    return data

def get_doc_labels(data):
    """Get document-level labels (1 if any token is anomalous)."""
    return [1 if any(l == 1 for l in labs) else 0 for labs in data['labels']]

def check_data(data):
    """Assert data properties match the paper."""
    n_docs = len(data['tokens'])
    doc_labels = get_doc_labels(data)
    n_normal = sum(1 for l in doc_labels if l == 0)
    n_anom = sum(1 for l in doc_labels if l == 1)
    
    assert n_docs == 300, f"Expected 300 docs, got {n_docs}"
    assert n_normal == 270, f"Expected 270 normal docs, got {n_normal}"
    assert n_anom == 30, f"Expected 30 anomalous docs, got {n_anom}"
    
    total_tokens = sum(len(t) for t in data['tokens'])
    total_pos = sum(sum(l for l in labs) for labs in data['labels'])
    print(f"Data check: {n_docs} docs, {n_normal} normal, {n_anom} anomalous")
    print(f"Total tokens: {total_tokens}, positive tokens: {total_pos}, rate: {total_pos/total_tokens:.4f}")
    
    return data

def split_data(data, seed=0):
    """
    Split data: 50% of normal docs for training, rest (normal + all anomalous) for test.
    Returns train_docs, test_docs, train_token_embeddings_info, test_token_embeddings_info
    """
    doc_labels = get_doc_labels(data)
    normal_indices = [i for i, l in enumerate(doc_labels) if l == 0]
    anom_indices = [i for i, l in enumerate(doc_labels) if l == 1]
    
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    rng.shuffle(normal_indices)
    
    n_train = len(normal_indices) // 2
    train_indices = normal_indices[:n_train]
    test_indices = normal_indices[n_train:] + anom_indices
    
    print(f"Split with seed {seed}: {len(train_indices)} train docs, {len(test_indices)} test docs")
    
    # Verify training set has no anomalous tokens
    for i in train_indices:
        assert all(l == 0 for l in data['labels'][i]), f"Train doc {i} has anomalous tokens!"
    
    return train_indices, test_indices, data

if __name__ == '__main__':
    data = load_grammar()
    check_data(data)
    train_idx, test_idx, data = split_data(data, seed=0)
    print(f"Train indices: {train_idx[:5]}...")
    print(f"Test indices: {test_idx[:5]}...")

"""
BERT-base-uncased embedding extraction with max pooling over subwords.
"""
import torch
import numpy as np
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel
from tqdm import tqdm

def get_model_and_tokenizer(model_name='bert-base-uncased', device=None):
    if device is None:
        device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = model.to(device).eval()
    return model, tokenizer, device

def embed_documents(model, tokenizer, documents_tokens, device, max_length=128, batch_size=32):
    """
    Embed a list of tokenized documents.
    documents_tokens: list of list of str (word tokens)
    Returns: list of dicts, one per document, each containing:
        - 'embeddings': np.array of shape (n_words, 768)
        - 'tokens': list of str
        - 'labels': list of int (or None)
    """
    results = []
    
    # Flatten all sentences for batch processing
    all_sentences = [' '.join(tokens) for tokens in documents_tokens]
    
    with torch.no_grad():
        for i in tqdm(range(0, len(all_sentences), batch_size), desc="Embedding"):
            batch_texts = all_sentences[i:i+batch_size]
            batch_tokens = documents_tokens[i:i+batch_size]
            
            encoded = tokenizer(
                batch_texts,
                padding=True,
                truncation=True,
                max_length=max_length,
                return_tensors='pt'
            )
            
            input_ids = encoded['input_ids'].to(device)
            attention_mask = encoded['attention_mask'].to(device)
            
            outputs = model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask)
            last_hidden = outputs.last_hidden_state  # (batch, seq_len, 768)
            
            for b in range(len(batch_texts)):
                seq_len = attention_mask[b].sum().item()
                word_ids = encoded.word_ids(batch_index=b)
                
                # Get subword embeddings for this sentence
                subword_embs = last_hidden[b, :seq_len].cpu().numpy()  # (seq_len, 768)
                
                # Max pool over subwords to get word embeddings
                word_embs = []
                current_word_idx = None
                current_subwords = []
                
                for pos, wid in enumerate(word_ids):
                    if wid is None:
                        continue
                    if wid != current_word_idx:
                        if current_subwords:
                            word_embs.append(np.max(np.stack(current_subwords), axis=0))
                        current_word_idx = wid
                        current_subwords = [subword_embs[pos]]
                    else:
                        current_subwords.append(subword_embs[pos])
                
                if current_subwords:
                    word_embs.append(np.max(np.stack(current_subwords), axis=0))
                
                word_embs = np.stack(word_embs) if word_embs else np.zeros((0, 768))
                
                # Align with gold tokens
                gold_tokens = batch_tokens[b]
                n_gold = len(gold_tokens)
                n_word_embs = word_embs.shape[0]
                
                if n_word_embs != n_gold:
                    # This can happen if tokenization differs from gold tokenization
                    # For now, truncate or pad to match
                    if n_word_embs > n_gold:
                        word_embs = word_embs[:n_gold]
                    else:
                        # Pad with zeros
                        pad = np.zeros((n_gold - n_word_embs, word_embs.shape[1]))
                        word_embs = np.vstack([word_embs, pad])
                
                results.append({
                    'embeddings': word_embs,
                    'tokens': gold_tokens,
                })
    
    return results

if __name__ == '__main__':
    model, tokenizer, device = get_model_and_tokenizer()
    print(f"Model on {device}")
    
    # Quick test
    test_tokens = [['Hello', 'world', '!']]
    results = embed_documents(model, tokenizer, test_tokens, device)
    print(f"Test result shape: {results[0]['embeddings'].shape}")
    print(f"Test tokens: {results[0]['tokens']}")

"""
Adapter for TokenCore memory bank detector.
"""
import sys
import os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', 'repo'))

from TokenCore import TokenCore
import numpy as np

def build_memory_bank(train_embeddings):
    """
    Build memory bank from normal training token embeddings.
    train_embeddings: np.array of shape (n_tokens, embed_dim)
    Returns: fitted TokenCore model
    """
    model = TokenCore(n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max')
    model.fit(train_embeddings)
    return model

def score_tokens(model, test_embeddings):
    """
    Score test tokens using the fitted memory bank.
    Higher distance = more anomalous.
    Returns: np.array of shape (n_tokens,) with anomaly scores
    """
    scores = model.decision_function(test_embeddings)
    return scores

if __name__ == '__main__':
    # Quick test
    X_train = np.random.randn(100, 768).astype(np.float32)
    X_test = np.random.randn(50, 768).astype(np.float32)
    
    model = build_memory_bank(X_train)
    scores = score_tokens(model, X_test)
    print(f"Train shape: {X_train.shape}, Test shape: {X_test.shape}")
    print(f"Scores shape: {scores.shape}, min: {scores.min():.4f}, max: {scores.max():.4f}")

"""
Evaluation metrics: AUROC and AUPRC at token and document level.
"""
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score

def compute_token_metrics(token_scores, token_labels):
    """
    Compute token-level AUROC and AUPRC.
    token_scores: np.array of shape (n_tokens,)
    token_labels: np.array of shape (n_tokens,) with 0/1
    """
    # Filter out any NaN scores
    mask = ~np.isnan(token_scores)
    scores = token_scores[mask]
    labels = token_labels[mask]
    
    if len(np.unique(labels)) < 2:
        # Not enough classes
        return None, None
    
    auroc = roc_auc_score(labels, scores)
    auprc = average_precision_score(labels, scores)
    return auroc, auprc

def compute_doc_metrics(doc_scores, doc_labels):
    """
    Compute document-level AUROC and AUPRC.
    doc_scores: np.array of shape (n_docs,)
    doc_labels: np.array of shape (n_docs,) with 0/1
    """
    if len(np.unique(doc_labels)) < 2:
        return None, None
    
    auroc = roc_auc_score(doc_labels, doc_scores)
    auprc = average_precision_score(doc_labels, doc_scores)
    return auroc, auprc

def aggregate_doc_scores(token_scores_per_doc):
    """
    Aggregate token scores to document scores by mean.
    token_scores_per_doc: list of np.arrays, one per document
    Returns: np.array of shape (n_docs,)
    """
    return np.array([scores.mean() if len(scores) > 0 else 0.0 for scores in token_scores_per_doc])

if __name__ == '__main__':
    # Test with synthetic data
    np.random.seed(42)
    labels = np.array([0]*900 + [1]*100)
    scores = np.random.randn(1000) + labels * 0.5
    
    auroc, auprc = compute_token_metrics(scores, labels)
    print(f"Token AUROC: {auroc:.4f}, AUPRC: {auprc:.4f}")
    
    doc_labels = np.array([0]*90 + [1]*10)
    doc_scores = np.random.randn(100) + doc_labels * 0.5
    auroc_d, auprc_d = compute_doc_metrics(doc_scores, doc_labels)
    print(f"Doc AUROC: {auroc_d:.4f}, AUPRC: {auprc_d:.4f}")

"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import numpy as np
import torch

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'repo'))

from data_grammar import load_grammar, check_data, split_data
from embed_bert import get_model_and_tokenizer, embed_documents
from detector import build_memory_bank, score_tokens
from evaluate import compute_token_metrics, compute_doc_metrics, aggregate_doc_scores

def main():

    parser.add_argument('--datasets', default='grammar', choices=['grammar'])
    parser.add_argument('--seed', type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument('--smoke', action='store_true')
    parser.add_argument('--max_length', type=int, default=128)
    parser.add_argument('--batch_size', type=int, default=32)
    parser.add_argument('--torch_threads', type=int, default=8)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    torch.set_num_threads(args.torch_threads)
    
    # Load data
    data = load_grammar()
    check_data(data)
    
    # Split
    train_idx, test_idx, data = split_data(data, seed=args.seed)
    
    if args.smoke:
        # Use only a small subset
        train_idx = train_idx[:8]
        test_idx = test_idx[:2] + train_idx[8:]  # Keep some anomalous
        test_idx = test_idx[:10]
        print(f"SMOKE MODE: using {len(train_idx)} train docs, {len(test_idx)} test docs")
    
    # Prepare documents
    train_tokens = [data['tokens'][i] for i in train_idx]
    train_labels = [data['labels'][i] for i in train_idx]
    test_tokens = [data['tokens'][i] for i in test_idx]
    test_labels = [data['labels'][i] for i in test_idx]
    
    # Get BERT model
    model, tokenizer, device = get_model_and_tokenizer()
    print(f"Using device: {device}")
    
    # Embed training documents
    print("Embedding training documents...")
    train_results = embed_documents(model, tokenizer, train_tokens, device, 
                                     max_length=args.max_length, batch_size=args.batch_size)
    
    # Build memory bank from normal training tokens
    train_embeddings_list = []
    for res in train_results:
        train_embeddings_list.append(res['embeddings'])
    X_train = np.vstack(train_embeddings_list) if train_embeddings_list else np.zeros((0, 768))
    print(f"Memory bank size: {X_train.shape[0]} tokens")
    
    # Embed test documents
    print("Embedding test documents...")
    test_results = embed_documents(model, tokenizer, test_tokens, device,
                                    max_length=args.max_length, batch_size=args.batch_size)
    
    # Score test tokens
    test_scores_per_doc = []
    test_labels_flat = []
    doc_labels = []
    
    for i, res in enumerate(test_results):
        X_test = res['embeddings']
        if X_test.shape[0] == 0:
            scores = np.array([])
        else:
            scores = score_tokens(None, X_test)  # We'll fit below... wait, need to fit first
        test_scores_per_doc.append(scores)
        test_labels_flat.extend(test_labels[i])
        doc_labels.append(1 if any(l == 1 for l in test_labels[i]) else 0)
    
    # Actually, we need to fit the model first, then score
    # Let me restructure...
    
    # Build memory bank
    print("Building memory bank...")
    detector = build_memory_bank(X_train)
    
    # Score test tokens
    test_scores_per_doc = []
    test_labels_flat = []
    doc_scores_list = []
    doc_labels = []
    
    for i, res in enumerate(test_results):
        X_test = res['embeddings']
        if X_test.shape[0] == 0:
            scores = np.array([])
        else:
            scores = score_tokens(detector, X_test)
        test_scores_per_doc.append(scores)
        test_labels_flat.extend(test_labels[i])
        doc_scores_list.append(scores.mean() if len(scores) > 0 else 0.0)
        doc_labels.append(1 if any(l == 1 for l in test_labels[i]) else 0)
    
    test_labels_flat = np.array(test_labels_flat)
    doc_scores = np.array(doc_scores_list)
    doc_labels = np.array(doc_labels)
    
    # Compute metrics
    token_auroc, token_auprc = compute_token_metrics(np.concatenate(test_scores_per_doc), test_labels_flat)
    doc_auroc, doc_auprc = compute_doc_metrics(doc_scores, doc_labels)
    
    print(f"\n=== Results (seed={args.seed}, smoke={args.smoke}) ===")
    print(f"Token AUROC: {token_auroc:.4f}" if token_auroc is not None else "Token AUROC: N/A")
    print(f"Token AUPRC: {token_auprc:.4f}" if token_auprc is not None else "Token AUPRC: N/A")
    print(f"Doc AUROC: {doc_auroc:.4f}" if doc_auroc is not None else "Doc AUROC: N/A")
    print(f"Doc AUPRC: {doc_auprc:.4f}" if doc_auprc is not None else "Doc AUPRC: N/A")
    
    # Write results
    os.makedirs('results', exist_ok=True)
    metrics = {
        'token_auroc': float(token_auroc) if token_auroc is not None else None,
        'token_auprc': float(token_auprc) if token_auprc is not None else None,
        'doc_auroc': float(doc_auroc) if doc_auroc is not None else None,
        'doc_auprc': float(doc_auprc) if doc_auprc is not None else None,
        'n_train_docs': len(train_idx),
        'n_test_docs': len(test_idx),
        'n_bank_tokens': int(X_train.shape[0]),
        'n_test_tokens': int(len(test_labels_flat)),
        'n_positive_tokens': int(test_labels_flat.sum()),
        'seed': args.seed,
        'smoke': args.smoke,
        'dataset': 'grammar'
    }
    
    with open('results/metrics.json', 'w') as f:
        json.dump(metrics, f, indent=2)
    
    print(f"\nResults written to results/metrics.json")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

                # Get subword embeddings for this sentence
                subword_embs = last_hidden[b, :seq_len].cpu().numpy()  # (seq_len, 768)
                
                # Max pool over subwords to get word embeddings
                word_embs = []
                current_word_idx = None
                current_subwords = []
                
                for pos, wid in enumerate(word_ids):
                    if wid is None:
                        continue
                    if wid != current_word_idx:
                        if current_subwords:

                        current_word_idx = wid

                    else:

                if current_subwords:
                    word_embs.append(np.max(np.stack(current_subwords), axis=0))
                
                word_embs = np.stack(word_embs) if word_embs else np.zeros((0, 768))
                
                # Align with gold tokens
                gold_tokens = batch_tokens[b]
                n_gold = len(gold_tokens)
                n_word_embs = word_embs.shape[0]

"""
Alignment check: print gold word tokens vs produced word units and subword spans.
"""
import sys
import os
os.chdir(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..'))

sys.path.insert(0, 'src')
sys.path.insert(0, 'repo')

import numpy as np
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

# Load data
data = np.load('repo/data/grammar.npy', allow_pickle=True).item()

# Load tokenizer
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased')

# Check first 5 documents
print("=== Alignment Check: Gold Tokens vs BERT Word Units ===\n")
for doc_idx in range(5):
    tokens = data['tokens'][doc_idx]
    labels = data['labels'][doc_idx]
    
    # Tokenize with BERT
    encoded = tokenizer(tokens, is_split_into_words=True, truncation=True, max_length=128)
    word_ids = encoded.word_ids(batch_index=0)
    subwords = tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(encoded['input_ids'])
    
    # Group subwords by word index
    word_units = []
    current_word = None
    current_subwords = []
    
    for i, wid in enumerate(word_ids):
        if wid is None:
            # Special token
            if current_word is not None:
                word_units.append((current_word, current_subwords))
                current_word = None
                current_subwords = []
            continue
        
        if wid != current_word:
            if current_word is not None:
                word_units.append((current_word, current_subwords))
            current_word = wid
            current_subwords = [subwords[i]]
        else:
            current_subwords.append(subwords[i])
    
    if current_word is not None:

"""
Run multi-seed evaluation for bert-base-uncased on Grammar dataset.
"""
import sys
import os
os.chdir(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..'))

sys.path.insert(0, 'src')
sys.path.insert(0, 'repo')

import json
import numpy as np
import torch
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score

from data_grammar import load_grammar, split_data, get_doc_labels
from embed_bert import get_model_and_tokenizer, embed_documents
from detector import build_memory_bank, score_tokens

def compute_token_metrics(token_scores, token_labels):
    mask = ~np.isnan(token_scores)
    scores = token_scores[mask]
    labels = token_labels[mask]
    
    if len(np.unique(labels)) < 2:
        return None, None
    
    auroc = roc_auc_score(labels, scores)
    auprc = average_precision_score(labels, scores)
    return auroc, auprc

def compute_per_doc_token_auroc(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc):
    aurocs = []
    for scores, labels in zip(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc):
        if len(scores) == 0:
            continue
        if len(np.unique(labels)) < 2:
            continue
        aurocs.append(roc_auc_score(labels, scores))
    if len(aurocs) == 0:
        return None
    return np.mean(aurocs)

def compute_per_doc_token_auprc(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc):
    auprcs = []
    for scores, labels in zip(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc):
        if len(scores) == 0:
            continue
        if len(np.unique(labels)) < 2:
            continue
        auprcs.append(average_precision_score(labels, scores))
    if len(auprcs) == 0:
        return None
    return np.mean(auprcs)

def main():
    # Load data
    data = load_grammar()
    doc_labels = get_doc_labels(data)
    
    # Get BERT model (load once)
    model, tokenizer, device = get_model_and_tokenizer('bert-base-uncased')
    print(f"Using device: {device}, backbone: bert-base-uncased")
    
    results = {}
    
    for seed in [0, 1, 2]:
        print(f"\n=== Seed {seed} ===")
        
        # Split data
        train_idx, test_idx, data = split_data(data, seed=seed)
        
        # Embed training documents
        train_tokens = [data['tokens'][i] for i in train_idx]
        train_results = embed_documents(model, tokenizer, train_tokens, device, max_length=128, batch_size=32)
        X_train = np.vstack([res['embeddings'] for res in train_results])
        
        # Embed test documents
        test_tokens = [data['tokens'][i] for i in test_idx]
        test_results = embed_documents(model, tokenizer, test_tokens, device, max_length=128, batch_size=32)
        
        # Build memory bank
        detector = build_memory_bank(X_train)
        
        # Score test tokens
        test_scores_per_doc = []
        test_labels_per_doc = []
        test_labels_flat = []
        doc_scores_list = []
        doc_labels_list = []
        
        for i, res in enumerate(test_results):
            X_test = res['embeddings']
            if X_test.shape[0] == 0:
                scores = np.array([])
            else:
                scores = score_tokens(detector, X_test)
            test_scores_per_doc.append(scores)
            test_labels_per_doc.append(np.array(res['labels']))
            test_labels_flat.extend(res['labels'])
            doc_scores_list.append(scores.mean() if len(scores) > 0 else 0.0)
            doc_labels_list.append(1 if any(l == 1 for l in res['labels']) else 0)
        
        test_labels_flat = np.array(test_labels_flat)
        doc_scores = np.array(doc_scores_list)
        doc_labels_arr = np.array(doc_labels_list)
        
        # Compute metrics
        token_auroc_micro, token_auprc_micro = compute_token_metrics(np.concatenate(test_scores_per_doc), test_labels_flat)
        token_auroc_perdoc = compute_per_doc_token_auroc(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc)
        token_auprc_perdoc = compute_per_doc_token_auprc(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc)
        doc_auroc, doc_auprc = compute_token_metrics(doc_scores, doc_labels_arr)
        
        results[seed] = {
            'token_auroc_micro': float(token_auroc_micro) if token_auroc_micro is not None else None,
            'token_auprc_micro': float(token_auprc_micro) if token_auprc_micro is not None else None,
            'token_auroc_perdoc': float(token_auroc_perdoc) if token_auroc_perdoc is not None else None,
            'token_auprc_perdoc': float(token_auprc_perdoc) if token_auprc_perdoc is not None else None,
            'doc_auroc': float(doc_auroc) if doc_auroc is not None else None,
            'doc_auprc': float(doc_auprc) if doc_auprc is not None else None,
            'n_train_docs': len(train_idx),

            'n_bank_tokens': int(X_train.shape[0]),
            'n_test_tokens': int(len(test_labels_flat)),
            'n_positive_tokens': int(sum(test_labels_flat)),
        }

        print(f"  Token AUPRC (micro): {token_auprc_micro:.4f}" if token_auprc_micro is not None else "  Token AUPRC (micro): N/A")

"""
Reproduce TokenCore token-level AUROC on Grammar dataset (Claim C1).
Primary: bert-base-uncased with micro pooling.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import numpy as np
import torch
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score

# Add src to path
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'src'))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'repo'))

from data_grammar import load_grammar, split_data, get_doc_labels
from embed_bert import get_model_and_tokenizer, embed_documents
from detector import build_memory_bank, score_tokens

def compute_token_metrics(token_scores, token_labels):
    """Compute token-level AUROC and AUPRC."""
    mask = ~np.isnan(token_scores)
    scores = token_scores[mask]
    labels = token_labels[mask]
    
    if len(np.unique(labels)) < 2:
        return None, None
    
    auroc = roc_auc_score(labels, scores)
    auprc = average_precision_score(labels, scores)
    return auroc, auprc

def compute_per_doc_token_auroc(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc):
    """Compute token-level AUROC per document, then average."""
    aurocs = []
    for scores, labels in zip(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc):
        if len(scores) == 0:
            continue
        if len(np.unique(labels)) < 2:
            continue
        aurocs.append(roc_auc_score(labels, scores))
    if len(aurocs) == 0:
        return None
    return np.mean(aurocs)

def compute_per_doc_token_auprc(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc):
    """Compute token-level AUPRC per document, then average."""
    auprcs = []
    for scores, labels in zip(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc):
        if len(scores) == 0:
            continue
        if len(np.unique(labels)) < 2:
            continue
        auprcs.append(average_precision_score(labels, scores))
    if len(auprcs) == 0:
        return None
    return np.mean(auprcs)

def run_single_seed(data, doc_labels, model, tokenizer, device, seed, backbone):
    """Run a single seed evaluation."""
    # Split data
    train_idx, test_idx, data = split_data(data, seed=seed)
    
    # Embed training documents
    train_tokens = [data['tokens'][i] for i in train_idx]
    train_results = embed_documents(model, tokenizer, train_tokens, device, max_length=128, batch_size=32)
    X_train = np.vstack([res['embeddings'] for res in train_results])
    
    # Embed test documents
    test_tokens = [data['tokens'][i] for i in test_idx]
    test_results = embed_documents(model, tokenizer, test_tokens, device, max_length=128, batch_size=32)
    
    # Build memory bank
    detector = build_memory_bank(X_train)
    
    # Score test tokens
    test_scores_per_doc = []
    test_labels_per_doc = []
    test_labels_flat = []
    doc_scores_list = []
    doc_labels_list = []
    
    for i, res in enumerate(test_results):
        X_test = res['embeddings']
        doc_idx = test_idx[i]
        doc_token_labels = data['labels'][doc_idx]
        if X_test.shape[0] == 0:
            scores = np.array([])
        else:
            scores = score_tokens(detector, X_test)
        test_scores_per_doc.append(scores)
        test_labels_per_doc.append(np.array(doc_token_labels))
        test_labels_flat.extend(doc_token_labels)
        doc_scores_list.append(scores.mean() if len(scores) > 0 else 0.0)
        doc_labels_list.append(1 if any(l == 1 for l in doc_token_labels) else 0)
    
    test_labels_flat = np.array(test_labels_flat)
    doc_scores = np.array(doc_scores_list)
    doc_labels_arr = np.array(doc_labels_list)
    
    # Compute metrics
    token_auroc_micro, token_auprc_micro = compute_token_metrics(np.concatenate(test_scores_per_doc), test_labels_flat)
    token_auroc_perdoc = compute_per_doc_token_auroc(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc)
    token_auprc_perdoc = compute_per_doc_token_auprc(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc)
    doc_auroc, doc_auprc = compute_token_metrics(doc_scores, doc_labels_arr)
    
    return {
        'token_auroc_micro': float(token_auroc_micro) if token_auroc_micro is not None else None,
        'token_auprc_micro': float(token_auprc_micro) if token_auprc_micro is not None else None,
        'token_auroc_perdoc': float(token_auroc_perdoc) if token_auroc_perdoc is not None else None,
        'token_auprc_perdoc': float(token_auprc_perdoc) if token_auprc_perdoc is not None else None,
        'doc_auroc': float(doc_auroc) if doc_auroc is not None else None,
        'doc_auprc': float(doc_auprc) if doc_auprc is not None else None,
        'n_train_docs': len(train_idx),
        'n_test_docs': len(test_idx),
        'n_bank_tokens': int(X_train.shape[0]),
        'n_test_tokens': int(len(test_labels_flat)),
        'n_positive_tokens': int(sum(test_labels_flat)),
    }

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--datasets', default='grammar', choices=['grammar'])
    parser.add_argument('--seed', type=int, default=0, help='Primary seed (also runs seeds 0,1,2 for spread)')
    parser.add_argument('--smoke', action='store_true')
    parser.add_argument('--max_length', type=int, default=128)

    parser.add_argument('--aggregation_check', action='store_true', help='Print both micro and per-document AUROC variants')
    args = parser.parse_args()

"""
Reproduce TokenCore token-level AUROC on Grammar dataset (Claim C1).
Primary: bert-base-uncased with micro pooling.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import numpy as np
import torch
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score

# Add src to path
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'src'))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'repo'))

from data_grammar import load_grammar, check_data, split_data, get_doc_labels
from embed_bert import get_model_and_tokenizer, embed_documents
from detector import build_memory_bank, score_tokens

def compute_token_metrics(token_scores, token_labels):
    """Compute token-level AUROC and AUPRC."""
    mask = ~np.isnan(token_scores)
    scores = token_scores[mask]
    labels = token_labels[mask]
    
    if len(np.unique(labels)) < 2:
        return None, None
    
    auroc = roc_auc_score(labels, scores)
    auprc = average_precision_score(labels, scores)
    return auroc, auprc

def compute_per_doc_token_auroc(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc):
    """Compute token-level AUROC per document, then average."""
    aurocs = []
    for scores, labels in zip(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc):
        if len(scores) == 0:
            continue
        if len(np.unique(labels)) < 2:
            continue
        aurocs.append(roc_auc_score(labels, scores))
    if len(aurocs) == 0:
        return None
    return np.mean(aurocs)

def compute_per_doc_token_auprc(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc):
    """Compute token-level AUPRC per document, then average."""
    auprcs = []
    for scores, labels in zip(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc):
        if len(scores) == 0:
            continue
        if len(np.unique(labels)) < 2:
            continue
        auprcs.append(average_precision_score(labels, scores))
    if len(auprcs) == 0:
        return None
    return np.mean(auprcs)

def run_single_seed(data, doc_labels, model, tokenizer, device, seed, backbone):
    """Run a single seed evaluation."""
    # Split data
    train_idx, test_idx, data = split_data(data, seed=seed)
    
    # Embed training documents
    train_tokens = [data['tokens'][i] for i in train_idx]
    train_results = embed_documents(model, tokenizer, train_tokens, device, max_length=128, batch_size=32)
    X_train = np.vstack([res['embeddings'] for res in train_results])
    
    # Embed test documents
    test_tokens = [data['tokens'][i] for i in test_idx]
    test_results = embed_documents(model, tokenizer, test_tokens, device, max_length=128, batch_size=32)
    
    # Build memory bank
    detector = build_memory_bank(X_train)
    
    # Score test tokens
    test_scores_per_doc = []
    test_labels_per_doc = []
    test_labels_flat = []
    doc_scores_list = []
    doc_labels_list = []
    
    for i, res in enumerate(test_results):
        X_test = res['embeddings']
        doc_idx = test_idx[i]
        doc_token_labels = data['labels'][doc_idx]
        if X_test.shape[0] == 0:
            scores = np.array([])
        else:
            scores = score_tokens(detector, X_test)
        test_scores_per_doc.append(scores)
        test_labels_per_doc.append(np.array(doc_token_labels))
        test_labels_flat.extend(doc_token_labels)
        doc_scores_list.append(scores.mean() if len(scores) > 0 else 0.0)
        doc_labels_list.append(1 if any(l == 1 for l in doc_token_labels) else 0)
    
    test_labels_flat = np.array(test_labels_flat)
    doc_scores = np.array(doc_scores_list)
    doc_labels_arr = np.array(doc_labels_list)
    
    # Compute metrics
    token_auroc_micro, token_auprc_micro = compute_token_metrics(np.concatenate(test_scores_per_doc), test_labels_flat)
    token_auroc_perdoc = compute_per_doc_token_auroc(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc)
    token_auprc_perdoc = compute_per_doc_token_auprc(test_scores_per_doc, test_labels_per_doc)
    doc_auroc, doc_auprc = compute_token_metrics(doc_scores, doc_labels_arr)
    
    # Log mean token scores for anomalous vs normal test docs
    anom_doc_scores = []
    norm_doc_scores = []
    for i, (scores, label) in enumerate(zip(test_scores_per_doc, doc_labels_list)):
        if len(scores) > 0:
            mean_score = scores.mean()
            if label == 1:
                anom_doc_scores.append(mean_score)
            else:
                norm_doc_scores.append(mean_score)
    
    mean_anom_score = np.mean(anom_doc_scores) if anom_doc_scores else None
    mean_norm_score = np.mean(norm_doc_scores) if norm_doc_scores else None
    
    return {
        'token_auroc_micro': float(token_auroc_micro) if token_auroc_micro is not None else None,
        'token_auprc_micro': float(token_auprc_micro) if token_auprc_micro is not None else None,
        'token_auroc_perdoc': float(token_auroc_perdoc) if token_auroc_perdoc is not None else None,
        'token_auprc_perdoc': float(token_auprc_perdoc) if token_auprc_perdoc is not None else None,
        'doc_auroc': float(doc_auroc) if doc_auroc is not None else None,
        'doc_auprc': float(doc_auprc) if doc_auprc is not None else None,
        'n_train_docs': len(train_idx),
        'n_test_docs': len(test_idx),
        'n_bank_tokens': int(X_train.shape[0]),
        'n_test_tokens': int(len(test_labels_flat)),
        'n_positive_tokens': int(sum(test_labels_flat)),
        'mean_anom_doc_score': float(mean_anom_score) if mean_anom_score is not None else None,
        'mean_norm_doc_score': float(mean_norm_score) if mean_norm_score is not None else None,
    }

import sys
import os
os.chdir(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..'))

sys.path.insert(0, 'src')
sys.path.insert(0, 'repo')

import numpy as np
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

# Load tokenizer and model
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased')
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased')
device = 'cpu'
model = model.eval()

# Test sentences
test_tokens = [
    ['I', 'go', 'to', 'the', 'store', 'everyday', '.'],
    ['She', 'don', "'", 't', 'like', 'apples', '.'],
    ['The', 'cat', 'is', 'sleeping', '.'],
    ['He', 'are', 'a', 'good', 'student', '.'],
    ['I', 'has', 'a', 'pen', '.']
]

# Method 1: Batch processing (my embed_bert.py)
with torch.no_grad():
    encoded = tokenizer(test_tokens, is_split_into_words=True, padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=128, return_tensors='pt')
    input_ids = encoded['input_ids'].to(device)
    attention_mask = encoded['attention_mask'].to(device)
    outputs = model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask)
    last_hidden = outputs.last_hidden_state
    
    batch_results = []
    for b in range(len(test_tokens)):
        seq_len = attention_mask[b].sum().item()
        word_ids = encoded.word_ids(batch_index=b)
        subword_embs = last_hidden[b, :seq_len].cpu().numpy()
        
        word_embs = []
        current_word_idx = None
        current_subwords = []
        
        for pos, wid in enumerate(word_ids):
            if wid is None:
                continue
            if wid != current_word_idx:
                if current_subwords:
                    word_embs.append(np.max(np.stack(current_subwords), axis=0))
                current_word_idx = wid
                current_subwords = [subword_embs[pos]]
            else:
                current_subwords.append(subword_embs[pos])
        
        if current_subwords:
            word_embs.append(np.max(np.stack(current_subwords), axis=0))
        
        word_embs = np.stack(word_embs) if word_embs else np.zeros((0, 768))
        batch_results.append(word_embs)

# Method 2: Single sentence processing (align.py style)
single_results = []
with torch.no_grad():
    for tokens in test_tokens:
        encoded = tokenizer(tokens, is_split_into_words=True, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, padding=False)
        input_ids = encoded['input_ids'].to(device)
        attention_mask = encoded['attention_mask'].to(device)
        outputs = model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask)
        last_hidden_state = outputs.last_hidden_state
        
        word_ids = encoded.word_ids(batch_index=0)
        sentence_data = []
        previous_word_idx = None
        current_subwords = []
        current_token = None
        current_label = None
        current_positions = []
        
        for token_position, word_idx in enumerate(word_ids):
            if word_idx is None:
                continue
            if word_idx != previous_word_idx:
                if current_subwords:
                    avg_emb = np.max(np.stack(current_subwords), axis=0)
                    sentence_data.append({
                        "token": current_token,
                        "embedding": avg_emb,
                        "label": current_label,
                        "subword_position": current_positions,
                    })
                current_token = tokens[word_idx]
                current_label = None
                current_subwords = [last_hidden_state[0, token_position, :].cpu().numpy()]
                current_positions = [token_position]
            else:
                current_subwords.append(last_hidden_state[0, token_position, :].cpu().numpy())
                current_positions.append(token_position)
            previous_word_idx = word_idx
        
        if current_subwords:
            avg_emb = np.max(np.stack(current_subwords), axis=0)
            sentence_data.append({
                "token": current_token,
                "embedding": avg_emb,
                "label": current_label,
                "subword_position": current_positions,
            })
        
        emb = np.array([item['embedding'] for item in sentence_data])
        single_results.append(emb)

# Compare
print("=== Batch vs Single Sentence Embedding Comparison ===\n")
for i, (b, s, tokens) in enumerate(zip(batch_results, single_results, test_tokens)):
    print(f"Doc {i}: {tokens}")
    print(f"  Batch shape: {b.shape}, Single shape: {s.shape}")
    if b.shape == s.shape:
        diff = np.abs(b - s).max()
        print(f"  Max diff: {diff:.10f}")
        if diff < 1e-6:
            print("  ✓ MATCH")
        else:
            print("  ✗ MISMATCH")
    else:
        print("  ✗ SHAPE MISMATCH")
    print()

"""
Execute authors' path verbatim and compare variants.
"""
import sys
import os
os.chdir(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..'))

sys.path.insert(0, 'src')
sys.path.insert(0, 'repo')

import json
import numpy as np
import torch
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

# Import authors' code
from TokenCore import TokenCore
from align import extract_word_embeddings

def split_anomaly_data(tokens, sentence_labels, labels, seed=0):
    """
    Split data into train/test following the paper's protocol:
    50% normal documents for training, rest (normal + anomalous) for testing.
    """
    np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # Find normal and anomalous document indices
    normal_idx = [i for i, label in enumerate(sentence_labels) if label == 0]
    anom_idx = [i for i, label in enumerate(sentence_labels) if label == 1]
    
    # Shuffle normal indices
    np.random.shuffle(normal_idx)
    
    # Split normal: 50% train, 50% test
    n_train_normal = len(normal_idx) // 2
    train_normal_idx = normal_idx[:n_train_normal]
    test_normal_idx = normal_idx[n_train_normal:]
    
    # Test set = remaining normal + all anomalous
    test_idx = test_normal_idx + anom_idx
    
    # Extract tokens and labels
    X_train = [tokens[i] for i in train_normal_idx]
    y_train = [sentence_labels[i] for i in train_normal_idx]
    z_train = [labels[i] for i in train_normal_idx]
    
    X_test = [tokens[i] for i in test_idx]
    y_test = [sentence_labels[i] for i in test_idx]
    z_test = [labels[i] for i in test_idx]
    
    return X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test

def run_authors_pipeline(data, backbone='bert-base-uncased', drop_punctuation=False):
    """
    Run the authors' pipeline exactly as in the notebook.
    """
    tokens = data['tokens']
    labels = data['labels']
    sentence_labels = [1 if any(labs) else 0 for labs in labels]
    
    # Split
    X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test = split_anomaly_data(tokens, sentence_labels, labels, seed=0)
    
    # Load model and tokenizer
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(backbone)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(backbone)
    device = 'cpu'
    model = model.eval()
    
    # Extract embeddings using authors' function
    train_data = extract_word_embeddings(
        model=model,
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
        all_tokens=X_train,
        all_labels=z_train,
        model_name=backbone,
        local_cache_dir=None,
        device=device
    )
    
    test_data = extract_word_embeddings(
        model=model,
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
        all_tokens=X_test,
        all_labels=z_test,
        model_name=backbone,
        local_cache_dir=None,
        device=device
    )
    
    # Flatten embeddings and labels
    X_train_flat = np.array([item['embedding'] for sent in train_data for item in sent])
    z_train_flat = [item['label'] for sent in train_data for item in sent]
    
    X_test_flat = np.array([item['embedding'] for sent in test_data for item in sent])
    z_test_flat = [item['label'] for sent in test_data for item in sent]
    
    # Optionally drop punctuation-only units
    if drop_punctuation:
        # Identify punctuation-only tokens in test set
        import string
        punct_mask = []
        for sent in test_data:
            for item in sent:
                token = item['token']
                is_punct = all(c in string.punctuation for c in token)
                punct_mask.append(not is_punct)
        punct_mask = np.array(punct_mask)
        
        X_test_flat = X_test_flat[punct_mask]
        z_test_flat = [l for l, m in zip(z_test_flat, punct_mask) if m]
    
    # Fit TokenCore (authors call it TextCore but we use TokenCore)
    model_det = TokenCore(n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max')
    model_det.fit(X_train_flat)
    scores = model_det.decision_function(X_test_flat)
    
    # Compute metrics
    auroc = roc_auc_score(z_test_flat, scores)
    auprc = average_precision_score(z_test_flat, scores)
    
    return auroc, auprc, X_train_flat, X_test_flat, z_test_flat, train_data, test_data

def print_anomalous_doc_details(data):
    """Print details of anomalous documents."""
    tokens = data['tokens']

            print(f"  Full text: {' '.join(toks)}")
            print()
    
    print(f"Total: {total_pos} anomalous tokens, {total_neg} normal tokens across all anomalous docs")

"""
Execute authors' path verbatim and compare variants.

import sys
import os
import io
import contextlib

os.chdir(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..'))

sys.path.insert(0, 'src')
sys.path.insert(0, 'repo')

import json
import numpy as np
import torch
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

# Import authors' code
from TokenCore import TokenCore
from align import extract_word_embeddings

def split_anomaly_data(tokens, sentence_labels, labels, seed=0):
    """
    Split data into train/test following the paper's protocol:
    50% normal documents for training, rest (normal + anomalous) for testing.
    """
    np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # Find normal and anomalous document indices
    normal_idx = [i for i, label in enumerate(sentence_labels) if label == 0]
    anom_idx = [i for i, label in enumerate(sentence_labels) if label == 1]
    
    # Shuffle normal indices
    np.random.shuffle(normal_idx)
    
    # Split normal: 50% train, 50% test
    n_train_normal = len(normal_idx) // 2
    train_normal_idx = normal_idx[:n_train_normal]
    test_normal_idx = normal_idx[n_train_normal:]
    
    # Test set = remaining normal + all anomalous
    test_idx = test_normal_idx + anom_idx
    
    # Extract tokens and labels
    X_train = [tokens[i] for i in train_normal_idx]
    y_train = [sentence_labels[i] for i in train_normal_idx]
    z_train = [labels[i] for i in train_normal_idx]
    
    X_test = [tokens[i] for i in test_idx]
    y_test = [sentence_labels[i] for i in test_idx]
    z_test = [labels[i] for i in test_idx]
    
    return X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test

def run_authors_path(data, backbone='bert-base-uncased', drop_punctuation=False):
    """
    Run the authors' pipeline exactly as in the notebook.
    """
    tokens = data['tokens']
    labels = data['labels']
    sentence_labels = [1 if any(labs) else 0 for labs in labels]
    
    # Split
    X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test = split_anomaly_data(tokens, sentence_labels, labels, seed=0)
    
    # Load model and tokenizer
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(backbone)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(backbone)
    device = 'cpu'
    model = model.eval()
    
    # Extract embeddings using authors' function - suppress verbose output
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
        train_data = extract_word_embeddings(
            model=model,
            tokenizer=tokenizer,
            all_tokens=X_train,
            all_labels=z_train,
            model_name=backbone,
            local_cache_dir=None,
            device=device
        )
        
        test_data = extract_word_embeddings(
            model=model,
            tokenizer=tokenizer,
            all_tokens=X_test,
            all_labels=z_test,
            model_name=backbone,
            local_cache_dir=None,
            device=device
        )
    
    # Flatten embeddings and labels
    X_train_flat = np.array([item['embedding'] for sent in train_data for item in sent])
    z_train_flat = [item['label'] for sent in train_data for item in sent]
    
    X_test_flat = np.array([item['embedding'] for sent in test_data for item in sent])
    z_test_flat = [item['label'] for sent in test_data for item in sent]
    
    # Optionally drop punctuation-only units
    if drop_punctuation:
        import string
        punct_mask = []
        for sent in test_data:
            for item in sent:
                token = item['token']
                is_punct = all(c in string.punctuation for c in token)
                punct_mask.append(not is_punct)
        punct_mask = np.array(punct_mask)
        
        X_test_flat = X_test_flat[punct_mask]
        z_test_flat = [l for l, m in zip(z_test_flat, punct_mask) if m]
    
    # Fit TokenCore (authors call it TextCore but we use TokenCore)
    model_det = TokenCore(n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max')
    model_det.fit(X_train_flat)
    scores = model_det.decision_function(X_test_flat)
    
    # Compute metrics
    auroc = roc_auc_score(z_test_flat, scores)
    auprc = average_precision_score(z_test_flat, scores)
    
    return auroc, auprc, X_train_flat, X_test_flat, z_test_flat

"""
Run authors' exact path from demo.ipynb on Grammar dataset.
"""
import sys
import os
import io
import contextlib

os.chdir(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..'))

sys.path.insert(0, 'src')
sys.path.insert(0, 'repo')

import json
import numpy as np
import torch
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

# Import authors' code
from TokenCore import TokenCore
from align import extract_word_embeddings

def split_anomaly_data(tokens, sentence_labels, labels, seed=0):
    """
    Reconstruct eval.split_anomaly_data from the notebook.
    50% normal documents for training, rest (normal + anomalous) for testing.
    """
    np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # Find normal and anomalous document indices
    normal_idx = [i for i, label in enumerate(sentence_labels) if label == 0]
    anom_idx = [i for i, label in enumerate(sentence_labels) if label == 1]
    
    # Shuffle normal indices
    np.random.shuffle(normal_idx)
    
    # Split normal: 50% train, 50% test
    n_train_normal = len(normal_idx) // 2
    train_normal_idx = normal_idx[:n_train_normal]
    test_normal_idx = normal_idx[n_train_normal:]
    
    # Test set = remaining normal + all anomalous
    test_idx = test_normal_idx + anom_idx
    
    # Extract tokens and labels
    X_train = [tokens[i] for i in train_normal_idx]
    y_train = [sentence_labels[i] for i in train_normal_idx]
    z_train = [labels[i] for i in train_normal_idx]
    
    X_test = [tokens[i] for i in test_idx]
    y_test = [sentence_labels[i] for i in test_idx]
    z_test = [labels[i] for i in test_idx]
    
    return X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test

def main():
    # Load data exactly as notebook does
    data = np.load(r'repo\data\grammar.npy', allow_pickle=True)
    data = data.item()
    
    tokens = data['tokens']
    labels = data['labels']
    sentence_labels = [1 if any(labs) else 0 for labs in labels]
    
    # Split exactly as notebook
    X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test = split_anomaly_data(
        tokens, sentence_labels, labels, seed=0
    )
    
    print(f"Train: {len(X_train)} docs, Test: {len(X_test)} docs")
    print(f"Train normal docs: {sum(1 for y in y_train if y == 0)}, anomalous: {sum(1 for y in y_train if y == 1)}")
    print(f"Test normal docs: {sum(1 for y in y_test if y == 0)}, anomalous: {sum(1 for y in y_test if y == 1)}")
    
    # Extract embeddings exactly as notebook (bert-base-cased)
    model_name = 'bert-base-cased'
    device = 'cpu'
    
    # Suppress verbose output from align.py
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
        train_data = extract_word_embeddings(
            model=None,
            tokenizer=None,
            all_tokens=X_train,
            all_labels=z_train,
            model_name=model_name,
            local_cache_dir=None,
            device=device
        )
        
        test_data = extract_word_embeddings(
            model=None,
            tokenizer=None,
            all_tokens=X_test,
            all_labels=z_test,
            model_name=model_name,
            local_cache_dir=None,
            device=device
        )
    
    # Flatten exactly as notebook
    X_train_flat = np.array([item['embedding'] for sent in train_data for item in sent])
    z_train_flat = [item['label'] for sent in train_data for item in sent]
    
    X_test_flat = np.array([item['embedding'] for sent in test_data for item in sent])
    z_test_flat = [item['label'] for sent in test_data for item in sent]
    
    print(f"\nTrain embeddings: {X_train_flat.shape}, labels: {len(z_train_flat)}")
    print(f"Test embeddings: {X_test_flat.shape}, labels: {len(z_test_flat)}")
    print(f"Positive test tokens: {sum(z_test_flat)}, negative: {len(z_test_flat) - sum(z_test_flat)}")
    
    # Fit TextCore (use TokenCore since TextCore isn't in repo)
    model = TokenCore()
    model.fit(X_train_flat)
    score = model.decision_function(X_test_flat)
    
    # Compute metrics exactly as notebook
    roc_auc = roc_auc_score(z_test_flat, score)
    auprc = average_precision_score(z_test_flat, score)
    
    print(f"\n=== Authors' Exact Path (bert-base-cased) ===")
    print(f"Token AUROC: {roc_auc:.4f}")
    print(f"Token AUPRC: {auprc:.4f}")
    print(f"Target: 0.6371 ± 0.02")
    print(f"In band: {0.6171 <= roc_auc <= 0.6571}")
    
    # Save result
    output = {
        'authors_exact_path': {
            'backbone': 'bert-base-cased',
            'token_auroc': float(roc_auc),
            'token_auprc': float(auprc),
            'in_band': bool(0.6171 <= roc_auc <= 0.6571)
        },
        'target': 0.6371,
        'tolerance': 0.02
    }
    
    os.makedirs('results', exist_ok=True)
    with open('results/metrics.json', 'w') as f:
        json.dump(output, f, indent=2)
    
    print(f"\nResults saved to results/metrics.json")
    
    return roc_auc

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

audit_summary: The clean re-run exits 0 and computes C1 from scratch: BERT-base-uncased, max-pooled subword embeddings, a memory bank of all normal-training token embeddings, 1-NN Euclidean token scores, mean document aggregation, and a 50% normal-document train/test split. The measured Grammar token AUROC is 0.5772 ± 0.0183 over seeds 0-2, below the target 0.6371 ± 0.02; per-document mean AUROC is 0.5811 ± 0.0496, also below. The implementation matches the paper's stated method, but the paper is underspecified/inconsistent: the authors' released demo uses bert-base-cased and yields 0.6583, while the paper text specifies bert-base-uncased; other unstated choices (BERT layer, punctuation handling, normalization, split seed) can also shift the score. The six baselines (R8) are not implemented, so the comparative ranking claim is not verified. No scale-down or hard-coded result was found: all 300 documents and three seeds were used, and the target 0.6371 appears only as a pass/fail constant.
